title: Introduction and Overview
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Chapter 1 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: oneSCM is the central system for service contract and maintenance products. This guide shows **what oneSCM is used for**, which **roles** work together and how the **global standard** interacts with **local variants** per market (Chapter 1.1 to 1.6).

steps: Read **Goals and benefits** (1.1): oneSCM combines price information, quote, application, contract and management in one system.
Position the project (1.2): oneSCM replaces legacy systems and maps the contract process for **Cars and Vans** uniformly.
Identify your **role** (1.3 and 1.4) and the related chapters:
Dealer: Chapters 4 to 8 and 10
MO: Chapters 9 and 10
Market: Chapter 14
HQ: Chapter 15

right.text: ~~Country-specific deviations~~ from the Blueprint are only valid if they are documented and approved in the country deviation register (Chapter 20.6).

steps: Understand the **business domains** (1.5): customer, vehicle, product, contract, payment and document are interlinked.
Note **standard and deviation** (1.6): The Blueprint applies globally; country deviations are documented in the register (Chapter 20).

qa: What does oneSCM stand for?
For central Service Contract Management: quote, application, contract and management of service and maintenance products.
Does the handbook apply to Cars and Vans?
Yes. Division differences are described in Chapter 21, country differences in Chapter 20.
Where do I start as a new user?
With Chapter 2 (access) and Chapter 3 (navigation), then with the process chapter for your role.

steps: Open oneSCM via __RetailPortal__ or via the __direct link__. Login is via **Single Sign-on** (2.1).
After login, check your **market, division and dealership context** (2.4): A wrong context means wrong products and prices.
Match your **business role** against your **technical authorizations** (2.2). Missing menu items indicate missing roles.

right.text: ~~Authorizations are never granted by e-mail or verbal request.~~ Every role is requested, reviewed and approved via ALICE; the approval is documented traceably.

steps: If an authorization is missing, submit the **authorization request** via ALICE (2.3). In the dealership, the **ALICE dealership admin** grants access.
For access issues (2.5): clear the browser cache, log in again, then report a support case with user ID and screenshot.
Lock your session when away and never share your account with others (2.6).

After a role change, you need to log in again.

qa: Why can't I see the Contract Creation menu item?
The related role is missing. Request it via ALICE from your dealership admin.
How long does an approval take?
Approval is given by the responsible admin; you can see the current status in the authorization request.
Can I have multiple roles?
Yes, for example Dealer roles for Cars and Vans; the active context is shown in oneSCM.

steps: Start on the **start page** (3.1): The tiles lead to **Contract Creation**, **Application Management**, **Customer Management** as well as warranty packages and external portals.
Use **search and filters** (3.2): reference number, VIN, customer name or status narrow down lists. Columns such as "Actions" are reached via the horizontal slider.
Recognize the **interaction patterns** (3.3): step bar with check marks, toggles for optional entries, three-dot menu for actions, mandatory fields marked with an asterisk.
Place your case on the **process map** (3.4 and 3.5): price information → quote → application → contract.

right.text: ~~A green check mark in the step bar does not mean that the contract is active.~~ Only the contract status "active" after review and activation (Chapter 8) is binding.

steps: Take over **leads** from the CRM and return results (3.6); note the **system handovers** to OTR, VEGA and oneERP (3.7).
Read **status information** correctly (3.8): application status, signature status and contract status are separate values.
Set your **work context and language** (3.9); documents follow the market's language variant (Chapter 7.4).

qa: Where can I find a saved application again?
Under Contract Creation › Application Management via the reference number (Chapter 8.1).
What is the difference between a quote and an application?
The quote is non-binding price information; the application is saved, signed, reviewed and activated.
Can I use the interface in another language?
Yes, via the personal work context (3.9); contract documents follow the market's language variants.

steps: Select the **customer group** (4.1). "KAM-managed key accounts" only for individual price requests or FS 140+.
First **search** for the customer and select them; only create a new record if needed (4.2). Identification is based on:
Private customer: first and last name, phone number, e-mail address or Mercedes me ID
Business customer: company name, VAT ID
Check **mandatory data** and plausibility (4.3): address, contact details, legal form; errors block later checks.

right.text: ~~Contract holder and registered keeper of the vehicle must be identical.~~ A different contract holder is not permitted; only payer and invoice recipient may differ.

steps: Assign the **contract roles** (4.4): contract holder, payer, user, contact and invoice recipient may differ, but must be permitted per market.
Transfer data from **connected systems** (4.5, e.g. oneERP) instead of retyping it; check for **duplicates** and conflicts (4.6).
Maintain **partner and Dealer relationships** (4.7); new dealers go through **Dealer onboarding** (4.8).

Duplicates usually result from creating new records without searching first; the MO can reject them.
Personal data does not belong in comments or screenshots (Chapter 16.1).
When transferring data from external systems, the leading system is authoritative (Chapter 16.2).

qa: May the payer differ from the contract holder?
Yes, the payer and the invoice recipient may differ; the contract holder must be the registered keeper.
What to do about conflicting master data?
Do not overwrite; document the deviation and pass it to the leading system or to support (Chapter 4.6).
How is a new Dealer connected?
Via the partner process and the market's Dealer onboarding (Chapter 4.8).

steps: Click "**Create contract**" and select the **contract type** (5.1).
Depending on the phase, enter the appropriate **entry point** to load the vehicle data (5.2):
For a price indication: **model series**
From quote: OTR **deal ID**
From order: VerSO **order ID**
From production: **VIN**
Add **first registration**, **current mileage** or **license plate** (5.3). If these are not yet known, activate the toggle.
Select the **service/maintenance package** (5.4) and configure **payment interval, term, annual mileage** and, if applicable, **industry** (5.5).

right.text: ~~As soon as you click "Create application", you jump to customer data entry~~ and can only edit the contract again later. Check product, term and mileage beforehand.

bullets: **Dealer**: create and hand over quote
**Market**: provide products, prices and campaigns (Chapter 14)
**MO**: review for special approvals
Customer is created or assigned (Chapter 4)
Vehicle identifier is available: model series, OTR deal ID, VerSO order ID or VIN
Permitted products for market and division are known
☐  Entry point selected to match the phase
☐  Vehicle data loaded and mandatory fields checked
☐  Product, term and mileage match the customer's wishes
☐  Campaign permitted, price information generated
The payment intervals "one-time" and "monthly" are always available; other intervals depend on customer segment and term.
Model series with six, seven and eight digits are accepted; contingent products (sales logic "FRD Not Related") are found via the model series, not via the VIN (5.4).
If the identifier returns no products, check the first registration date and mileage: vehicles above the product's maximum age or maximum mileage receive no results (5.3).
Demonstrator and company cars count as used vehicles; only a pure maintenance package is possible for them.

steps: If available, add **technical options** and **additional services** and select **active campaigns** or **your own dealer discounts** (5.6). Check eligibility against the campaign description.
Check the contract details in the **payment plan** and generate the "**Price information**" preview (PDF) for quote purposes. Note the **quote validity** (5.7).
With "**Create application**" you hand over the quote to application creation (5.8, Chapter 6).

qa: Which identifier do I use before the order?
The model series for a price indication; from quote the OTR deal ID, from order the VerSO order ID.
Can I change a quote later?
Yes, until application creation; after that the change rules from Chapter 5.7 and 10.2 apply.
How long is a quote valid?
Validity depends on market requirements and price version (Chapter 5.7 and 14.9).

steps: Check **contract type and prerequisites** (6.1): vehicle, product and customer group must match the contract type.
Enter the **contract data** (6.2): mandatory fields are marked with an asterisk; missing entries block saving.
In the **payment plan** section, check the assignment of **customer, vehicle and product** (6.3) and use the **application preview** (PDF).
Read **validation messages** (6.4): red messages must be resolved; yellow notes allow you to continue.

right.text: ~~The payment interval can later only be changed to "one-time"~~; other changes require a new contract.

You activate a collective invoice during the customer data check via the toggle at the bottom of the page.

qa: Can I change the application after saving?
To a limited extent: first registration, license plate and documents via "Update" (Chapter 8.3); conditions require a new contract.
What does a special approval mean?
The application deviates from the standard and is reviewed by the MO before it can be activated (Chapter 9 and 12.4).
Where can I see the reference number?
In the overview after saving and in the first column of Application Management.

steps: Select **payment method and payment interval** (7.1) and define **payer and invoice recipient** (7.2).
Enter **bank details** and generate the **SEPA mandate** (7.3); for a collective invoice, activate the toggle.
Generate the **application preview** (PDF) and check the **language variant** of the documents (7.4).

right.text: ~~For contract review and activation, first registration, license plate and a copy of the ZB II must be available.~~ For the print variant, contract documents and SEPA mandate must be uploaded separately.

steps: Select the **signature type** (7.5 and 7.6):
**E-signature (QR code)**: customer scans the code, signs on mobile; filed automatically.
**Signature by e-mail**: link by e-mail, access with 4-digit SMS code; filed automatically.
**Print document**: handwritten signature, then scan and "Upload application".
For multiple signatories or changes, obtain the **signature again** (7.7).
Check **signature, document and application status** (7.8) before moving on to the activation check (Chapter 8).

With digital signing, the contract is sent to the customer automatically.
The print variant is suitable when several signatures are required or when no digital signature is possible.
Alternatively, the contract document can be opened on a computer via the link.

qa: The customer has no mobile number on file. What now?
The e-mail variant requires SMS verification; use the e-signature via QR code or the print variant.
Can a document be uploaded later?
Yes, via Application Management › Update › Communication (Chapter 8.3).
What happens with a re-signature?
The previous document is replaced; the signature status starts over (Chapter 7.7).

steps: Under **Contract Creation**, click "**Application Management**" and search for the application via the **reference number** (8.1).
Move the slider to the right to the "**Actions**" column, click "**…**" and select "**Update**".
Enter the **first registration date** and **license plate** (8.3).

right.text: ~~Uploading the ZB II is not a mandatory field in the system, but no activation takes place without the document.~~ Incorrect applications are rejected and the customer is informed.

Check the **result** (8.6): contract status "active" and feedback in Communication.
In case of **rejection**, Customer Management will contact you; correct the data and resubmit the application (8.7).

A service contract can be concluded up to 12 months and/or a maximum of 50,000 km after first registration, provided the vehicle has not yet received a service (exception: company and demonstrator vehicles with a previous owner).
The contract start corresponds to the date of first registration.
Status transitions are documented as a matrix in Appendix D.

qa: How long does activation take?
With complete data, automatic activation takes place promptly; manual reviews by Customer Management take correspondingly longer (8.5).
My application was rejected. What to do?
Read the rejection reason in Communication, correct the data and resubmit the application (8.7).
Can I filter by status?
Yes, Application Management offers filters by status, date and customer (8.1).

Completeness and plausibility of customer, vehicle, product, payment data, documents and signature (9.2 and 9.4).
Can the Dealer see the check status?
Yes, in Application Management as a status and in Communication as feedback.
How often can a re-check be done?
As often as corrections are submitted; every check is traceable in the history (9.5).

items: You **search for contracts**, change **contract, customer and payment data**, carry out **change of payer and transfer**, **suspend and reactivate**, extend or **close** contracts and use the **change history** (Chapter 10.1 to 10.8).

steps: Search for the contract via reference number, VIN or customer and check the **details** (10.1).
Change **contract, customer or payment data** via the permitted actions (10.2); the payment interval can later only be changed to "one-time".
Carry out a **change of payer** or **contract transfer** with the required evidence (10.3).
**Suspend** or **reactivate** for legitimate reasons (10.4).

right.text: ~~Changes to product, term or mileage require a new contract.~~ Cancellations and closures have financial consequences (Chapter 11.6) and are irreversible.

steps: Before the end of the term, create a **follow-up quote** or a **follow-up contract** (10.5).
For **termination, cancellation or closure**, check the **financial consequences** and secure the **closing evidence** (10.6 and 10.7).
Check the **change history** (10.8); every change is traceable with time, role and reason.
Check the **mileage history** and trigger the **mileage projection** when MIC data is missing (10.9); it is a reference value and does not end the contract.

Changes go through the MO Check according to Chapter 9.7.
A mileage from a workshop invoice above the contract mileage sets the status "expired by mileage" (10.6).
The history is the basis for reporting and governance (Chapter 16).

qa: Can I increase the mileage?
Not in the current contract; this requires a new contract or follow-up contract (10.2 and 10.5).
What is the difference between cancellation and termination?
Cancellation voids the contract, termination ends it at a set date; both have their own financial consequences (10.6 and 10.7).
Where can I see who changed something?
In the contract's change history (10.8).

title: Invoicing, Payment, Costs and Reports
footer: **Note**: This Quick Guide summarizes Chapter 11 of the oneSCM handbook. Details, screenshots and evidence can be found in the handbook.

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: You understand **invoicing and payment schedules**, distinguish **invoice and payment status**, handle **different invoice recipients and collective invoices**, know **cost management and claims**, **final settlement and corrections** and use **reporting and exports** (Chapter 11.1 to 11.8).

left.text: References to handbook chapters and systems are highlighted; e-mail addresses are provided as links.

steps: Check the contract's **payment schedule** (11.1): interval, amounts and due dates.
Distinguish **invoice status** (issued, cancelled) and **payment status** (open, paid, overdue) (11.2).
For a **different invoice recipient** or **collective invoice**, check the assignment from Chapter 7.2 (11.3).

right.text: ~~Invoice and payment status are separate values.~~ An issued invoice is not paid, and an incoming payment does not automatically change the contract status.

steps: Track **costs and claims** per contract (11.4) and the **workshop and supplier references** (11.5).
On closure, the **final settlement** takes place with **refund** or **correction** (11.6).
Use **reporting, filters and exports** for analyses (11.7) and hand over **deviations** to the department or support (11.8).

Accounting processing takes place in NEMESIS, payments via MPay, customer data via oneERP (Chapter 19.11 to 19.15).
When a workshop invoice is accepted, the system transfers the mileage into the contract's mileage history (10.9, 11.5).
Calculation examples for refunds are in Appendix I.2.

qa: Why is the contract "paid" but the invoice "open"?
Both statuses come from different systems and are updated at different times (11.2).
Who corrects an incorrect invoice?
The Finance department via the correction process; you hand over the case with the reference number (11.6 and 11.8).
Can I export reports?
Yes, via Reporting with filters and export (11.7), depending on your role.
